transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more, but... I guess I've just been having a little trouble with my eating lately? 

It's probably nothing major, I just... well, some days before my shift, I can barely manage to get down a coffee and a granola bar. And I've noticed my scrubs have been hanging pretty loose lately. I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, so I figured I should probably get it checked out... is that the right thing to do? I hope it was okay to come in for that.
When you have trouble eating before your shift, is it because you feel anxious or worried?

Oh, um... no, I don't think it's that. I mean, I hope I don't sound like I'm stressed out or can't handle my job—I really do fine at work, I promise. It's just... I don't know, I just don't really have much of a desire to eat? 

The thought of food just doesn't... it just doesn't appeal to me right now, I guess. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful answer. Am I explaining that okay? I just don't want you to think I'm letting things get to me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm, like, clinically depressed or anything. I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know a lot of people have it way worse than I do. But, um... I guess I have been feeling a little... off? 

It's just... most mornings, I wake up and there's this... this heavy, sort of hollow feeling in my chest. It's almost like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. But I still go in, and I do my job, I promise. I don't let it affect my patients. Is it normal to feel like that sometimes? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually enjoy less than before?

Um... well, I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I don't want to sound lazy or anything, I'm still keeping up with all my responsibilities at work. But... on my days off, I haven't been doing as much as I used to. 

I used to really like going for runs in Van Cortlandt Park, and I'd take my camera out to take photos... or I'd meet up with some friends to play chess. But lately, I just... I don't know, I tell myself there's really no point in going all the way out there. So I mostly just end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or looking over my budget spreadsheet. 

I know I should probably get out more, I'm trying to be better about it, I promise. It's just been a little hard to find the energy. Is that... does that make sense? I hope that answers your question okay.
Are you trying to lose weight?

Oh, no, no, definitely not trying to lose weight. I mean, I know I could probably stand to be a little healthier, but I'm not on a diet or anything like that. 

It's just... like I was saying, my eating has just gotten so off lately. Some days I realize I've barely gotten down a cup of coffee and maybe a granola bar before my whole shift is over. And... well, I have noticed my scrubs have been hanging a lot looser on me recently. 

I'm really not trying to starve myself or anything, I promise. I know it's important to keep my strength up for the patients. I just... the food just doesn't go down. Is it okay that I haven't been eating much? I don't want you to think I'm neglecting my health on purpose.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Oh, um... well, I really wouldn't want you to worry about me. I'm definitely not... I haven't made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I would never want to put that kind of burden on anyone, especially the people I work with. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes, when that heavy feeling is really bad, I do kind of catch myself just... wishing I wouldn't wake up in the morning. Or just thinking that maybe it would be easier if I could just... disappear? 

I know that sounds terrible, and I feel really guilty even saying it out loud because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. I'm really not trying to be dramatic, I promise. Is it... does that make me sound crazy? I just wanted to be honest with you since you asked.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, it's been a little while, I guess. I don't want to make it sound like I've been dragging my feet for ages or anything. I've still been showing up for all my shifts! 

But... if I really think about it... I think this all kind of started back when the clinic did that big overhaul of the EMR system and changed up our workflows. That ended up changing my hours, and... well, that was almost two years ago now. 

I know that's a long time to be feeling like this, and I probably should have said something sooner. I just kept thinking I'd adjust to the new schedule and bounce back, you know? I didn't want to be a bother or seem like I couldn't handle the changes at work. I hope it's okay that I waited this long to get help. I'm really trying to get it sorted out now, I promise.
Do you feel this all began because of the changes to your work schedule?

Um... well, it's hard to say for sure. I don't want to blame it all on work, because they've been really good to me there, and I know everyone has to deal with schedule changes sometimes. I really try to be flexible and go with the flow.

But... I guess that was just when I first started noticing that things felt off. Like, I couldn't seem to catch up on my sleep, and the heavy feeling just kind of settled in around then. I don't know if the schedule change actually *caused* it, or if it was just a coincidence that it happened at the same time. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses or complaining about my job. I really do like working there. Do you think a schedule change could do something like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
If your work schedule had never changed, do you think you would still be feeling this way?

Oh, um... wow, that's a really good question. I, uh... I really don't know. 

I'd like to think that if everything had just stayed the same, I'd be my usual self, you know? Just coming in, doing my job, being helpful. But... honestly, I'm not entirely sure. 

I guess it's possible this would have happened anyway? I don't want to point fingers at the clinic or the new system, because like I said, they've been wonderful to me. It might just be something wrong with me, regardless of the hours. 

I'm sorry, I know that's not a very helpful answer. I just really don't know for sure. Is it normal to not know what caused it? I hope I'm not making your job harder by not having a clear answer for that.
Even on days when work isn’t a problem, do you still wake up with that heavy, hollow feeling?

Um... yeah, I actually do. Even on my days off, or when everything is going perfectly fine at the clinic. 

I don't want to sound ungrateful, because I know I have a lot of good things going for me, but... yeah, most mornings I just wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling. It's almost like the whole day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work, or before I even get out of bed. 

I try really hard to just push through it and put on a smile, you know? I don't want to bring anyone else down. But it's just always there waiting for me when I wake up. I hope that makes sense? I know I shouldn't be feeling that way when there's no actual problem to be upset about.
During the past two years, has there been a period of at least two months when you felt back to your usual self?

Um... two months? Let me think... 

I really want to say yes, because I try so hard to just bounce back and be my normal, helpful self. And I definitely have days where I can smile and get through my shift without anyone noticing anything is wrong. I don't want you to think I'm just miserable all the time, because I really do try my best.

But... a whole two months straight of feeling completely normal? I don't... I don't think so. It feels like this heavy feeling has just been kind of... hanging around for a long time now. Even when I have a good week, it always seems to creep back in before a month goes by. 

I'm sorry, I wish I could give you a better answer. I know I should be able to shake this off better than I have been. Is it okay that I haven't had a long break from it like that? I hope I'm not doing something wrong that's making it stick around.
